name: Plan

require.label: resolve TODO/FIXME markers in the written sections

blurb: Phases from the feature DAG, then each feature decomposed into agent-ready issues.
prompt:
The features are a dependency DAG — run `bsc-plan feature list` to see every feature and its
`dependsOn`. Turn that into the buildable plan in two passes: (1) sequence the DAG into ordered
phases, then (2) decompose each feature, in dependency order, into agent-ready issues. Foundations
(features others depend on) come first; everything builds on top. When the issues are written, STOP
and ask the user to APPROVE. Leave no TODO / TBD / FIXME / XXX / TKTK markers — the gate blocks on
them.

Coordination is carried by the plan itself, not a separate graph: feature `dependsOn` is the coarse
roadmap, and each issue's `dependsOn` is the concrete build order the director and workers follow.
Where a real cross-feature contract exists (a shared schema/types/API), write it as a doc under
`contracts/<name>.md` — the director owns those and workers read them as the source of truth.

substeps.label: Sequence into phases
substeps.prompt:
Sequence the features into ordered phases — write `phases.json` (a JSON array of
`{"name","description"}`, each phase a crisp "done when"; no time estimates). Use the feature DAG
(`bsc-plan feature list`): a feature's `dependsOn` features must land in the SAME or an EARLIER
phase, never later — foundations first, user-facing capabilities on top. Phases span repos. Present
the phase order together with the dependency graph and get the user's APPROVAL before decomposing
any feature.

substeps.label: Decompose each feature
substeps.prompt:
Decompose ONE feature at a time, in dependency order (a feature's `dependsOn` features
should already be decomposed). For the CURRENT feature, run `bsc-plan feature get <slug>` to pull
its full spec, then break it into granular, agent-ready issues — one per call:
`echo '{"ref":"…","title":"…","phase":<n or name>,"stream":"<slug>","acceptance":["…"],"owns":["…"],"dependsOn":["…"],"labels":["…"]}' | bsc-plan add`
The feature is the parent: its issues carry its slug as `stream`. Each issue names the files/globs it
`owns`, its `acceptance` checklist, its `phase`, and a `dependsOn` that REALIZES the feature's
dependencies — point at the specific issue refs in the features this one builds on, so each coarse
feature edge becomes concrete issue dependencies. Define enough that an agent finishes WITHOUT
asking. `bsc-plan list --stream <slug>` reviews this feature's issues; `bsc-plan list` the whole
plan. Then move to the next feature in DAG order.
